sentences.text: Changyuraptor is a genus of predatory dinosaurs known for having four wings.
Feathers covered its entire body, including the forelimbs and hindlimbs, creating the appearance of two pairs of wings.
Its long, feathered tail featured end feathers reaching up to 29.27 centimeters in length.
This dinosaur is the largest known four-winged microraptorine, exceeding previous specimens in size by at least 60%.
Researchers believe the elongated tail feathers helped provide softer and safer landings.
The only known specimen was found in Early Cretaceous deposits 125 million years old in Liaoning Province, China.
The genus and species Changyuraptor yangi were formally described in 2014.
The generic name Changyuraptor combines the Chinese words for 'long feather' with the Latin word for 'robber'.
The specific name yangi honors the researcher Professor Yang Yandong.
Changyuraptor and related microraptorines provide evidence that dinosaurs evolved features like feathers, hollow bones, and possibly flight before birds did.
Changyuraptor belongs to the Microraptoria group of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs.
It is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
Additionally, it is classified within the subfamily Microraptorinae.
Changyuraptor lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
It inhabited moist temperate forests dominated by ginkgos and conifers, experiencing hot, dry summers and frosty winters.
